chunks: I stand witness that He is just and does justice; He is the arbiter Who decides (between right and wrong).
I also stand witness that Muḥammad is His slave. His Messenger and the Chief of His creatures.
Whenever Allāh divided the line of descent, He put him in the better one,
and therefore, no evil-doer ever shared with him nor was any vicious person his partner.
ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about the nobility of Prophet Muhammad's descent?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi presents this passage as a concise declaration of Muhammad’s (peace be upon him) absolute moral integrity, emphasizing that he was chosen from the best of humanity and remained free from the taint of major sins or the wicked. This aligns with the Shia doctrine of Ismah (infallibility), portraying him not merely as a messenger but as the exemplar of divine justice and wisdom. The text underscores his unique status as the 'Master of Servants,' linking his personal nobility directly to the broader cosmic order of divine selection.
